summary.text: Carol Hill-Evans is a Democratic state representative from York County who has represented Pennsylvania House District 95 since December 2016 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026. She chairs the House State Government Committee.

paragraphs.text: Carol Hill-Evans is a native of York City, was educated in the York City School District, and earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Business from Penn State York, according to her official biography.
Her prior work was in human resources, and she retired after 27 years from Caterpillar Inc.
She served nine years on York City Council, as both vice president and president.
Hill-Evans was elected to the state House on November 8, 2016, to represent the 95th Legislative District.
Her official biography says she chairs the State Government Committee and belongs to the Central Pennsylvania Delegation, and that she co-chairs the Bi-Partisan Women's Caucus.
The same biography lists issues she focuses on, including equitable education funding, economic development, homelessness, and resources for veterans and first-line defenders.
Ballotpedia lists her as having advanced from the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 99.4 percent of the vote; Jasmine Rivera is the Republican candidate in the general election.
